title: LILRB1 as a novel therapeutic target for CAR-T therapy in diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
abstract: Diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains a therapeutic challenge due to antigen escape and T cell exhaustion following anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy. Here, we identify leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor-B1 (LILRB1) as a clinically actionable CAR-T target. LILRB1 is widely enriched in nodal and extranodal DLBCL patient samples but exhibits minimal expression on early hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, offering a favorable therapeutic index. LILRB1 CAR-T cells demonstrated potent, antigen-dependent cytotoxicity against CD19-resistant tumors and mediated durable tumor clearance in xenograft models. To mitigate antigen heterogeneity, we generated LILRB1×CD19 tandem CAR-T cells, which significantly enhanced tumor control. However, long-term therapeutic durability was bounded by progressive T cell exhaustion, characterized by the upregulation of TIM3 and 2B4. To overcome this intracellular bottleneck, we evaluated pharmacologic blockade of nuclear receptor 4A1/2 (NR4A1/2) using the small-molecule ligand 1,1-bis(3'-indolyl) -(3,5-dichlorophenyl) methane (DIM-3,5-Cl2). DIM-3,5-Cl2 successfully reversed CAR-T cell exhaustion, restored polyfunctional cytokine release in vitro, and maximized tumor control and overall survival in stringent in vivo rechallenge models across both LILRB1 and CD19 CAR platforms. Together, these findings establish LILRB1 as a structurally stable CAR target and validate NR4A pharmacotherapy as a generalizable platform adjuvant to optimize adoptive immunotherapies.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
